findings.text: Strength: the first three paragraphs say what Athena is, what a study is, and why this page exists. A newcomer can say what they are looking at before the firstmate detail starts.
findings.source: header: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: Strength: the next action is linked from the top and repeated at the end, with a repo link, an install command and a sample request.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: The install step names no prerequisites, such as a Rust toolchain or the AI model access the lede implies. It also doesn't say what `athena ask` produces, so a newcomer can't tell whether they can run it.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The page shows off studies, but the only command it gives makes a change ("add a changelog"). A newcomer who wants a study like this of their own project isn't told how to get one.
findings.source: header lede vs Next steps: "turns a short request into a change to a code repository" … "Athena made this study of firstmate"

findings.text: Several terms the main flow depends on are never defined, either in "Words used first" or in the Glossary: "captain call", "endpoint", "unheld" and "durable record".
findings.source: Start here: "If the backlog item is still an open captain call, teardown reopens it"; t8: "a secondmate with no endpoint"; step 1: "unheld, unblocked item"

findings.text: The Glossary explains "mark" ("read") but not the "mechanism" and "prose-only" tags on every claim, so the reader can't tell how much weight each claim carries.

The same definitions appear in several places almost word for word (yolo, green/red, in scope, places). That makes the page long for a first visit and buries the short "Start here" section among the repeats.
findings.source: Words used first / Glossary: "yolo … A setting that decides who approves merges" (repeated in What firstmate is, step 5, t4, t10, Glossary)

findings.text: This finding describes the study's own internal process, which means little to a newcomer. Its "not run" tag doesn't match its content, which is about missed paths.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f3: "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths…"

findings.text: It points to a `studies/` folder with no link or repository, so a newcomer can't follow it.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data"
